about.text: Oaxaca cheese, also called quesillo or queso de hebra, is a white, semi-hard Mexican cow's-milk cheese first made in the state of Oaxaca. It is a pasta filata cheese: the curd is stretched into long ribbons that are rolled up like a ball of yarn, and it is stringy like string cheese or mozzarella.

how.text: Cultured, rennet-set curd is cooked, soured in its whey until it is ready, then kneaded in hot water until it stretches. The strand is pulled flat, cooled, salted and wound into a ball of twine, which is why Oaxaca cheese pulls apart in strings. The source gives no stretching-water temperature.
